claimText: Task dequeue operations must atomically transition the task record from available state to active execution state and establish a time-bounded lease within a single storage engine consistency boundary before returning payload to worker.
Superseded worker ownership must not authorize protected state transitions (completion, failure, retry) inside the storage engine.
Crash recovery sweepers must enforce a safety margin buffer or multi-phase mark-and-sweep delay exceeding the lease interval before re-enqueuing expired tasks.
Poison work must have bounded delivery attempts and be routed to dead-letter quarantine (DLQ) upon exceeding a maximum threshold.
Systems regulate message flow across process and network boundaries using explicit credit tokens, client-driven demand signaling, or TCP read suspension rather than unbounded internal memory buffers.
Storage engines experiencing I/O stalls or lock wait times exceeding a critical threshold must immediately reject incoming writes with explicit transient errors (SYSTEM_BUSY / Alarms).
Relational SQL queues must select candidate task rows using SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED or single-statement CTEs to allow concurrent lock-free dequeue across worker connections.
High-throughput storage engines write immutable sequential records aligned to physical block/sector boundaries (e.g., 4KB) using Direct I/O (O_DIRECT) or circular pre-allocated journals.
Multi-topic messaging systems decouple immutable sequential physical payload storage (CommitLog/Osiris) from lightweight logical queue index structures (ConsumeQueue/Radix-Trie/Offset Map).
Clustered broker groups replicating message logs or cluster state must enforce epoch/term validation on all mutations, rejecting operations from superseded leadership terms.
Message identity generators encoding timestamp prefixes (UUIDv7, Snowflake, GUID) must maintain strict monotonic ordering and reject or compensate for backward time drift.

Worker and broker shutdown sequences must trap OS termination signals, halt new task ingestion, allow in-flight tasks to drain up to a timeout, and requeue uncompleted tasks without incrementing attempt counters.
Task deduplication within an active sliding window must be enforced via storage-level uniqueness constraints (partial unique indexes or atomic key reservations) evaluated before task persistence.
Administrative control directives (cancellations, pauses) must propagate via dedicated out-of-band push channels (PubSub, LISTEN/NOTIFY, actor control messages) to preempt executing worker contexts.
Ownership fencing must guard every authoritative side-effecting state mutation, including domain result promotion or outbox emission, not only queue-row completion.
Lease/recovery SQL must evaluate time at the authoritative storage boundary; test-injection hooks or caller-supplied timestamps must not become production recovery clocks.
Durable attempt-start counters, handled-failure counters, and worker-loss/stall counters encode different guarantees and must not be collapsed in poison-payload retry policy.
Repeatable or scheduler-specific infinite-stall exemptions are not applicable to domains where every crashing payload must have bounded delivery attempts and DLQ routing.
Publish-path overload protection must bound admission waiters as well as admitted bytes/requests; otherwise resource exhaustion can move from buffers into waiter queues.

Worker-drain deadlines and broker-socket deadlines are separate shutdown contracts; renewers for in-flight work must survive soft stop until completion or explicit interrupt, while idle/slow clients need hard close deadlines.
